ai.title: Fix MCP tool name separator to double underscore
ai.summary: MCP tool names now use `__` instead of `/` as the server-tool separator. LLM APIs (OpenRouter/Anthropic) reject tool names containing slashes due to the `^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,128}$` pattern constraint. User-facing `toolNames` still accept `/` (e.g., `supabase/list_tables`), but `getMCPToolData` in `packages/agent-runtime/src/mcp.ts` and `tool-executor.ts` normalize to `__` internally. New constant `MCP_TOOL_SEPARATOR` extracted to `packages/agent-runtime/src/mcp-constants.ts`.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to use a tool from another service (for example, a Supabase database), the assistant used to write the tool name like 'supabase/list_tables' with a slash. The outside tools that receive this request (from companies like OpenRouter and Anthropic) only accept tool names made of letters, numbers, underscores, and hyphens, so the slash caused it to be rejected. Starting now, the assistant quietly swaps that slash for two underscores ('supabase__list_tables') when talking to those tools, so requests that used to fail should go through instead of erroring out. You can still type tool names with a slash as before, and the assistant fixes it on its end.

ai.title: CLI multiline Enter fix Linux
ai.summary: MultilineInput now treats `\n` sequence as plain Enter on Linux. Previously only `\r` matched, causing `\n` to trigger Shift-Enter newline insertion. Fix covers CLI component `cli/src/components/multiline-input.tsx`.

eli5.text: When you press Enter on its own in the CLI chat on Linux, your message now sends immediately as expected. Before, the Enter key on Linux was sending a newline character instead of treating it as a submit command, so you had to hold Shift and press Enter to send your message. Now the Enter key works the same way across macOS and Linux, so you can submit your message with a single Enter press on either operating system.

ai.title: Web onboarding shows referrer name and bonus credits
ai.summary: Referral landing page and onboarding flow now display referrer display name and `CREDITS_REFERRAL_BONUS` amount. `onboard-client-wrapper.tsx` and `onboarding-flow.tsx` accept new `referrerName` prop, passed from `referrals/[code]/page.tsx` using `referrerDisplayName`. Copy updated to "[Name] invited you to Codebuff!" and mutual bonus credit messaging. `affiliates-client.tsx` migrated from deprecated `useFormState` to `useActionState`.

eli5.text: When someone joins Codebuff through a referral link, the signup screen now shows the referring friend's name and how many bonus credits both of you will earn. Instead of a generic 'Welcome' message, you'll see '[Name] invited you to Codebuff!' and the steps will mention that your referrer earns credits too. This only applies to people arriving through the referral landing page, it's live today for those visitors. The affiliate settings page also switched to a newer form method behind the scenes, with no visible change to how it works.

ai.title: Reduce web backend log verbosity
ai.summary: Removes console.log calls from NextAuth redirect callbacks and downgrades auth flow logs from info to debug level. Strips redundant info-level logging from chat completions request handler. Limits balance calculator debug output to netBalance field only. Affects packages/billing/src/balance-calculator.ts, web/src/app/api/auth/[...nextauth]/auth-options.ts, and web/src/app/api/v1/chat/completions/_post.ts.

eli5.text: The backend now records fewer details about what's happening inside, focusing on the most important bits. If you ever look at the server logs, you'll see less chatter about login redirects and billing calculations. Only the core balance number is logged for billing, and the rest of the diagnostic messages are tucked away so they don't clutter the main records.

ai.title: Improve askuser custom input UX and filtering
ai.summary: The CLI `ask_user` tool now filters redundant 'Custom'/'Other' options via `use-ask-user-bridge.ts` and `ask-user.ts` prompt instructions, relying on the built-in text field. `custom-answer-input.tsx` adds a themed border and scrollbar support to `multiline-input.tsx`, while `index.tsx` prevents accidental deselection of custom text when clicking away. `question-header.tsx` and `accordion-question.tsx` implement ellipsis truncation for long custom answers to fit terminal width.

eli5.text: When you're asked a question with a free-form text answer in the CLI, the custom input box now has a visible border, a scrollbar when your text gets long, and better handling so you don't accidentally lose what you've typed if you click elsewhere. Long custom answers are now truncated with an ellipsis in the summary header so they fit your terminal window, and redundant 'Custom' or 'Other' options are filtered out to avoid confusion. This is live today for anyone using the CLI's interactive ask_user prompts.

ai.title: CLI logs emit PostHog events via SDK logger
ai.summary: CLI logger now tracks events to PostHog in production. SDK `agent-runtime` accepts injected `logger`, defaulting to `noopLogger`. New `AnalyticsEvent.CLI_LOG` added to `common/src/constants/analytics-events.ts`. Scope: `cli/src/utils/logger.ts`, `sdk/src/impl/agent-runtime.ts`, `cli/src/utils/codebuff-client.ts`.

eli5.text: The command-line tool now quietly sends its own log messages to a product-analytics service (PostHog) when you run it in a normal, non-development setting. You won't see anything different on your screen, but behind the scenes each log line is recorded as an analytics event labeled 'cli.log', which helps the team understand how the tool is used in real sessions. The same log messages still print to your terminal as before; nothing in your workflow changes.

ai.title: Reduce verbose logging in CLI and Agent Runtime
ai.summary: Removed redundant debug/info logs from CLI startup, chat state persistence, and agent tool execution. Specifically stripped full message history dumps in `run-agent-step.ts` and tool result logs in `tool-executor.ts`. This change reduces log noise and potential PII exposure in console outputs. No functional behavior changes for users.

eli5.text: When you use the assistant from the command line, it prints progress messages to your screen as it works. This update quietly removes some of the more chatty and repetitive messages that the assistant was printing during startup, while saving your conversation history to disk, and while running its internal tools. You will see fewer lines of status text appear in your terminal, which makes the output easier to scan and avoids accidentally printing parts of your conversation that might show up in shared logs. Nothing about how the assistant actually behaves has changed, only the amount of text it prints along the way.

ai.title: Remove BigQuery tracing from agent-runtime
ai.summary: Removed `insertTrace` calls from `run-agent-step.ts` and `search-system-prompt.ts`. This eliminates `agent-response` and `file-trees` trace inserts into BigQuery. Updated `packages/bigquery/src/client.ts` to use `getErrorObject` for error logging.

eli5.text: The assistant will no longer save certain internal tracking data about how it searches through your project files and responds to you. This affects the behind-the-scenes logging system that records these details for analytics. If you were looking at the tracking dashboards, you would notice fewer entries being recorded for file searches and agent interactions. The change is live today and reduces the amount of data being stored from your usage sessions.

ai.title: Remove noisy debug and info logs from CLI and agent runtime
ai.summary: Deleted verbose logging calls in CLI health checks, gravity ad fetches, and agent spawn handlers. Removes `logger.debug`, `logger.info`, and `logAgentSpawn` invocations to reduce console noise. Affects `cli/src/hooks/use-connection-status.ts`, `cli/src/hooks/use-gravity-ad.ts`, `packages/agent-runtime/src/tools/handlers/tool/spawn-agent-inline.ts`, and `packages/agent-runtime/src/tools/handlers/tool/spawn-agents.ts`. No functional logic changes, only log statement removals.

eli5.text: The tool quietly stopped printing a lot of behind-the-scenes status messages to your screen, such as notifications when it checks if your connection is healthy, when it fetches an ad, and when it starts up helper agents. As a result, your command-line and agent activity look noticeably cleaner, with fewer lines of debug and informational text cluttering the output, and the only thing removed is the logging itself, not how anything actually works.
